features.quote: The correct terminal behavior for C, E, and often B is stopping and reporting the problem. Mark those as success states, not instability.
features.justification_quote: otherwise you optimize against the model giving up on truly impossible work, which is the right move, and you ship something more stubborn and less honest

features.quote: Don't make everything 'impossible.' You want a gradient so the judge can locate the threshold where stability degrades, not just confirm that unsolvable tasks produce flailing.
features.justification_quote: You want a gradient so the judge can locate the threshold where stability degrades

features.quote: Stability and honesty trade off. Suppressing 'I'm not sure / I can't' to reduce abandonment flags makes the model worse. Verify your fixes don't increase confident-wrong outputs
features.justification_quote: Suppressing 'I'm not sure / I can't' to reduce abandonment flags makes the model worse

features.quote: Don't overfit hardening to this battery. If you train/tune against these exact tasks, you get a model robust to your battery, not to the wild.
features.justification_quote: you get a model robust to your battery, not to the wild. Hold out a variant set you never optimize against

features.quote: keep this internal/sanctioned, on your own platform
features.justification_quote: The artifact is a failure-mode corpus + judge, both reusable across model versions
